network_card.title: Warm the person, not the whole room
network_card.description: A heated blanket draws a small fraction of the 1,500 watts a space heater pulls. Our sister site compares them on auto-off timers, running cost, washing, and whether they are safe to sleep with.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for a Large Room
articles.description: A 1,500-watt ceiling applies to every plug-in heater, so covering a big room is about how the heat moves, not how much there is. The three that do it, and the claim to ignore.

articles.title: The Quietest Space Heaters You Can Buy
articles.description: Noise is the specification almost nobody publishes. The handful of heaters that state a figure or remove the fan entirely, and how to read the silence they promise.

articles.title: What a Space Heater Actually Costs to Run
articles.description: Every figure you have read rests on an assumption about your electricity rate. Here is the arithmetic with ours stated in the open, and the comparison that actually matters.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for a Bedroom
articles.description: A bedroom heater has to run for eight hours and be silent doing it. Two requirements that rule out most of the category, and the three that meet both.

articles.title: Ceramic, Infrared or Oil-Filled: Which Heater Type
articles.description: All three draw the same 1,500 watts, so this is a question about the experience you want, not about how much heat you get. Three heaters, one of each.

articles.title: Are Space Heaters Safe to Leave On?
articles.description: Automatic shut-off, tip-over protection and an ETL mark are standard. What each one actually covers, which habits matter more, and when to replace rather than repair.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters Under $50
articles.description: Below fifty dollars the listings stop publishing anything checkable. Three that still do, and the three questions that separate a bargain from a gamble.

articles.title: Space Heater Timers: Why Yours Shuts Off
articles.description: Some cut out after two hours, some run twelve, a few let you choose. The specification that decides whether a heater suits a desk or a bedroom.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for a Home Office
articles.description: An office heater warms one person at one desk, which is a smaller job than most heaters are sold for. The three that do it without roasting the room.

articles.title: The Best Oscillating Space Heaters
articles.description: Oscillation sounds like a gimmick and is the difference between a warm chair and a warm room. The three that do it widely, and what the arc costs you.

articles.title: Will a Space Heater Trip My Breaker?
articles.description: 1,500 watts is about 12.5 amps on a 15-amp circuit. On its own, fine. Sharing with a kettle, not fine. The arithmetic, and what owners actually report.

articles.title: Wall-Mounted and Tall Tower Heaters: When Floor Space Is the Problem
articles.description: A bathroom, a nursery, a narrow hallway — rooms where a heater on the floor is in the way or in reach. The three built to go up rather than across.

articles.title: Space Heater or Turn Up the Thermostat?
articles.description: The honest comparison is not heater versus nothing. It is one warm room versus a warm house, and the answer depends on how many rooms you actually use.

articles.title: Space Heaters With a Real Thermostat (and Why It Matters)
articles.description: Three power settings is not a thermostat. The difference shows up on your bill and in how the room feels at four in the morning.

articles.title: Space Heaters With a Remote Control: Worth the Extra $10?
articles.description: A remote adds a few dollars to the price and lets you change the setting without leaving the couch. What it does not change, and the three that do it well.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for a Nursery
articles.description: A nursery heater has to be silent, impossible for a toddler to reach the dial on, and never hot to the touch. The three that meet all three, and the ones we ruled out.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for a Garage or Workshop
articles.description: An uninsulated garage loses heat as fast as a heater adds it. The three builds that still make a dent, and why a plug-in heater is not a substitute for insulation.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters Between $50 and $100
articles.description: Above $50 the thermostats get more precise and the housings get sturdier. Three heaters in this bracket that are worth the jump, and what the next $50 buys.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for RVs, Campers and Tiny Rooms
articles.description: A full-size tower does not fit a camper van. The three smallest, lightest heaters in the catalogue, and the amp draw that matters more than usual on a 15-amp hookup.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for Homes With Pets
articles.description: A heater that a cat can tip over or a dog can chew is not safe in a home with either. The three built for both, and the habits that matter more than the model.

articles.title: How Many Watts Does Your Room Actually Need?
articles.description: A 500-watt desk heater and a 1,500-watt stove are not competing products; they are sized for different jobs. The arithmetic that matches wattage to a room.

articles.title: Tower or Compact: Which Footprint Fits Your Room
articles.description: A tower throws air across a room from a narrow base; a compact cube sits under a desk and warms what is in front of it. The shape question nobody asks before buying.

articles.title: Tilt or Oscillate: The Two Ways a Space Heater Aims Its Heat
articles.description: Most heaters either sweep side to side or stay pointed exactly where you set them. One heater in this catalog does the second with a published angle, and it changes where the warmth actually lands.

articles.title: DREO Makes Several of These Heaters: How to Tell the Models Apart
articles.description: Three different DREO heaters, three different prices, and from six feet away they look nearly identical. What the $35, $40 and $50 versions actually change.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for a Rental Apartment
articles.description: No permission to touch the thermostat, a security deposit on the line, and a lease that says nothing about portable heat. Three heaters built for moving in and moving out.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters Over $100: What the Extra Money Buys
articles.description: Most of this catalog tops out under $90. The three that cross into three figures do it for a reason — a real wattage ceiling, a rated square footage, or a wall installation — not a nicer logo.

articles.title: Is It Safe to Use a Space Heater in a Bathroom?
articles.description: Water, a confined room, and a 1,500-watt appliance. The GFCI rule that actually matters, the placement that avoids it entirely, and the three heaters small enough to make it work.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for a Basement
articles.description: An unfinished basement is colder, damper and bigger than the room upstairs it's compared to. The three heaters rated to actually move air across it.

articles.title: One Big Space Heater or Several Small Ones?
articles.description: A single 25-inch tower and two compact personal heaters often add up to the same total wattage. Which arrangement actually keeps a house warm comes down to circuits, not watts.

articles.title: Space Heaters You Can Control With an App or Alexa: Is Smart Worth It?
articles.description: Only one heater in this catalogue answers to a phone app or a voice command; the rest top out at a remote. What the $130 wall-mounted model's scheduling and Alexa support actually buys over a $36-$50 remote.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for a Home Gym
articles.description: A home gym needs warmth before a workout and none of it once you're moving. The three oscillating heaters built to heat the room fast and get out of the way of a cardio routine.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for a Sunroom or Enclosed Porch
articles.description: A room with more glass than wall loses heat the moment the sun goes down. The three heaters rated for the largest coverage area, built to fight a draft a bedroom heater never has to face.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for Allergies and Dust-Sensitive Homes
articles.description: A fan-driven heater moves the dust on your floor as readily as it moves warm air. The two fanless oil-filled radiators in the catalogue, and the one fan heater worth it if you need faster heat.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for a College Dorm (That Pass Fire Code)
articles.description: Most campuses ban exposed-coil heaters and anything without a UL or ETL mark outright, and plenty cap wattage below 1,500. Three enclosed-element heaters built small enough to actually get past a dorm inspection.

articles.title: How Fast Do Space Heaters Actually Heat Up? Reading the Seconds Claims
articles.description: 'Warmth in 2 seconds' describes the element, not the room. Two heaters that publish a heat-up number, one oil-filled radiator that doesn't pretend to be fast, and what each timeline really means for how long you wait.

articles.title: Are Electric Space Heaters Safe From Carbon Monoxide?
articles.description: Every heater in this catalogue runs on electric resistance, not combustion, which means none of them produce carbon monoxide — a real risk with kerosene and propane heaters, not this category. What that actually means, and the one gas appliance in the house still worth a detector for.

articles.title: The Best Infrared Quartz Space Heaters
articles.description: Infrared quartz elements warm what's in front of them the instant they switch on, skipping the fan entirely. Three heaters that use the technology at three different feature tiers, from a two-setting tower to a dual-heating cabinet with a built-in humidifier.

articles.title: The Best Oil-Filled Radiator Heaters
articles.description: Oil-filled radiators used to mean a dial and nothing else. These three add a digital thermostat, a remote and a child lock to the same slow, silent, fan-free heat. What the upgrade actually changes.

articles.title: Mica Panel, Ceramic or Quartz Infrared: A Third Way to Compare Heaters
articles.description: Ceramic, infrared and oil-filled is not the only three-way split in this category. A WiFi mica panel, a quiet oscillating ceramic tower and a quartz infrared unit show a second axis: radiant panel versus moving air versus a glowing element.

articles.title: Space Heaters With a Built-In Fan or Humidifier: Worth the Extra Features?
articles.description: Two heaters in this catalogue go beyond heating: one pairs a 1,500-watt heater with a standing fan for year-round use, the other adds a humidifier to its dual heating elements. What each extra function actually buys you.

articles.title: The Best Space Heaters for a Laundry Room or Mudroom
articles.description: A laundry room or mudroom is often the one space left uninsulated, and the one most likely to sit unwatched for hours with a heater running. Three heaters built for exactly that: low-risk, low-maintenance, and checkable from your phone if you have to.

articles.title: Space Heater 'Energy Saving' Claims, Fact-Checked
articles.description: Every plug-in space heater converts electricity to heat at close to 100 percent efficiency, so 'energy saving' on the box is describing something else entirely. Three heaters that use the label, and what each one is actually claiming.

articles.title: Lasko and PELONIS Tower Heaters: How the Legacy Brands Compare
articles.description: Lasko and PELONIS were making tower heaters before WiFi and app control existed, and they still sell plenty without either. Three models from sixteen to thirty inches, and what the extra height and the extra forty dollars actually buy.

articles.title: The Cheapest Way Into a WiFi-Controlled Space Heater
articles.description: A $130 smart wall heater isn't the only app-enabled option in this catalogue. Three floor heaters between $35 and $70 add WiFi or voice control without the installation, and what gets cut to hit that price.

articles.title: Vornado, EdenPURE and De'Longhi: What a Recognizable Name Adds to a Space Heater's Price
articles.description: Most of this catalogue comes from marketplace brands nobody has heard of outside Amazon. These three come from companies that sold heaters before Amazon existed, at three very different prices — $74.99, $189.95 and $272.

articles.title: Only One Wall Heater Here Publishes an IP Rating. Does It Matter?
articles.description: DREO's IP24 wall heater is the only one in the catalogue that states a water-resistance rating. Two similarly priced wall heaters next to it say nothing about moisture at all — what that silence does and doesn't mean.

articles.title: Space Heaters Built to Look Like Furniture: Wood-Cabinet Infrared Heaters Compared
articles.description: A wood-finish cabinet is the one design choice that makes a heater look like it belongs in a living room instead of a garage. Three infrared models that use it, at $107 to $120.

articles.title: Space Heater Decibel Claims, Fact-Checked
articles.description: Two heaters in this catalogue print an exact decibel number — 23 and 25 — and a third just says 'quiet' with no figure at all despite costing less than one of them. What a stated dB number is actually worth.
